title: Compare CPU before, during and after
goal: Observe one short-lived CPU worker without imposing a performance threshold.
challenge: Record bounded before/during/after samples, identify the actual worker and supervisor, explain interval versus lifetime CPU measurements, and verify the worker ended. Do not start a second worker or signal a PID saved from an older shell.

steps.explanation: Create a unique private guest workspace. Retain its printed path; repeat starts a new workspace, never overwrites old evidence. Stop if creation/change-directory fails.
steps.expected: A new /home/learner/capacity-cpu.XXXXXX directory. All files below are guest-local.

steps.explanation: Record an idle/context baseline before creating work.
steps.expected: First row is a since-boot average; later rows are interval samples.

steps.command: if [ -z "$(jobs -p)" ]; then timeout -k 2s 12s bash -c 'while :; do :; done' & worker=$!; sleep 1; birth=$(awk '{print $22}' "/proc/$worker/stat"); cpu=$(ps -o pid= --ppid "$worker"); ps -o pid,ppid,pcpu,stat,args -p "$worker" --ppid "$worker"; timeout -k 2s 8s vmstat 1 4 > during.txt; wait "$worker"; result=$?; printf "supervisor=%s child=%s status=%s\n" "$worker" "$cpu" "$result" > worker.txt; cat during.txt worker.txt; else printf "Finish existing shell jobs before another worker.\n"; fi
steps.explanation: Read this entire compound command first, then type it as one line. One busy Bash is supervised for 12 seconds; do not pause midway. The shell waits for that exact child.
steps.expected: Supervisor normally returns 124 after its timer. One busy worker may change CPU observations; differences are not guaranteed.

steps.explanation: Observe after the bounded worker has ended.
steps.expected: Load averages can decay slowly; other activity may remain.

steps.command: if [ -n "$worker" ] && jobs -p | grep -qx "$worker" && [ "$(awk '{print $22}' "/proc/$worker/stat" 2>/dev/null)" = "$birth" ]; then kill -TERM "$worker"; fi; if [ -n "$worker" ]; then wait "$worker" 2>/dev/null || :; fi
steps.explanation: Safe interruption cleanup: only the still-owned job with the same recorded start tick can receive TERM. wait reaps the exact child. Repeating cleanup is safe; no PID files survive logout.
steps.expected: No lesson worker remains. If interrupted before birth was captured, the timer still ends the worker; wait for it.

steps.explanation: Retain actual identities and exit result, not a fixed PID.
steps.expected: No live lesson job remains; unavailable output after interruption is inconclusive, not a failure to fabricate.

hints: Type the whole timed compound line without stopping to read between commands.
One worker on a two-vCPU guest may not consume every CPU; do not enforce 50% or 100%.
Only signal a current shell child with matching /proc start ticks; otherwise wait for the timer.
review: I recorded before/during/after and actual child identities.
I checked timer completion or documented an interruption honestly.
I distinguished CPU utilization, lifetime averages and load.
coverage: Partial 200.1 CPU measurements/correlation, reinforcing 103.5 process inspection. Completion records self-review, not verified guest assessment; there is no score.
